Substitute the point $A(2, 2)$ into the curve equation:
$$2 = k\left( 2^3 - 7(2^2) + 12(2) \right) = k(8 - 28 + 24) = 4k \implies k = \frac{1}{2}$$

hints: Since $y = 5 = x$, it lies on $y = x$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the $y$-value on the curve when $x = 5$:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}\left( 5^3 - 7(5^2) + 12(5) \right) = \frac{1}{2}(125 - 175 + 60) = \frac{1}{2}(10) = 5$$

Confirm intersection with the line $y = x$:
$$\text{Since } y = 5 = x, \text{ the curve meets the line } y = x \text{ at } (5, \, 5)$$

Set up the integral for the area between the curve and the line $y = x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^2 \left[ \frac{1}{2}(x^3 - 7x^2 + 12x) - x \right]\,dx = \int_0^2 \left( \frac{1}{2}x^3 - \frac{7}{2}x^2 + 5x \right)\,dx$$
